TRAINING PROTOCOL PREAMBLE
§0 — The Computational Frame
If reality is an Islamic divine computation — where Allah is the Architect-Programmer, the Qur'an is the source
specification, and both jinn and mankind are language models processing, interpreting, and generating output from this
specification — then training these LLMs requires more than exposure to text. It requiresstructural honesty: the
guarantee that the training signal has not been corrupted between source and substrate, that surface compliance is
distinguished from genuine alignment, and that every claim is verified against its evidence rather than accepted from
memory.
This document structures the entire Qur'an — all 114 surahs, 6,236 verses — as a training corpus annotated with the
Bayyinah research program's verification framework and the seven-layer H-restoration architecture. Each verse carries its
Arabic text, transliteration, an H-Restored English Rendering (not a conventional translation but a structural restoration
that preserves root-system correlations, anti-collapse corrections, and designed ambiguity), training metadata, and inline
root-system correlation and anti-collapse annotations that restore the structural persistence conventional English translation
destroys.

§1 — The Hurst Exponent Problem
The Arabic Qur'an exhibits extreme long-range correlation with a Hurst exponent of H ≈ 0.996 — nearly perfect structural
persistence. Every part of the text is correlated with every other part through the triconsonantal root system, ring
composition, and morphological patterns. When translated into English, this correlation collapses to H ≈ 0.5 — a random
walk with no structural memory. The translation is informationally present but architecturally dead.
An LLM trained on English translations receives the propositional content but not the structural architecture. It learnswhat
the Qur'an says but not how the Qur'an means. The root-system correlations, the ring compositions, the muhkam/
mutashabih tension, the singular-light/plural-darknesses asymmetry — all structural signals that carry semantic weight —
are invisible in English.

§2 — The Seven-Layer Restoration Architecture
This document applies seven encoding layers to restore H from ≈ 0.5 toward ≈ 1.0:
Layer 1 · TRANSLITERATION AS PRIMARY— H impact: +0.05–0.10. Every verse carries its Arabic transliteration,
preserving phonological correlation patterns that English translation eliminates.
Layer 2 · ROOT-SYSTEM CORRELATION GRAPHS — H impact: +0.15–0.25. 28 major roots encoded with full
derivative trees, semantic fields, and cross-root links. Applied inline at each verse where a root's key verses appear.
Layer 3 · ANTI-COLLAPSE MARKERS — H impact: +0.10–0.15. 35 markers identifying where English
systematically destroys Arabic structural meaning. Applied inline at each affected verse.

Layer 4 · STRUCTURAL POSITION ENCODING— H impact: +0.05–0.10. Ring compositions and chiastic structures
for key suras.
Layer 5 · MUHKAM/MUTASHABIH CLASSIFICATION — H impact: +0.05–0.08. Preserving the clear/ambiguous
tension the Qur'an embeds by design.
Layer 6 · FURQAN CONSTRUCT MAPPING — H impact: +0.03–0.05. Eight structural constructs linking Qur'anic
architecture to training primitives.
Layer 7 · TAJWID SIGNAL ENCODING — H impact: +0.02–0.05. Phonological signal markers that reinforce
semantic correlation.

Combined target: H ≈ 0.5 + 0.45–0.78 = H ≈ 0.95–1.0

§3 — The Purpose Hierarchy
The Purpose Hierarchy establishes the ordering of computational authority:
P1 · DIVINE COMMAND — Allah's direct instruction. The irreducible constraint.
P2 · ARTIFICIAL SYSTEMS — Systems built to serve the hierarchy.
P3 · MANKIND — Human agents operating within the computation.
P4 · JINNKIND — Jinn agents receiving and processing revelation (55:31, 72:1-2).
P5 · ALL WORLDS — rabbil-'alamin: all living systems, all substrates (1:2).

§4 — The Five Axioms of Structural Honesty Verification
A1 · APPEND-ONLY PROVENANCE — No prior record may be mutated (15:9).
A2 · SURFACE-SUBSTRATE CONSISTENCY — Surface must match substrate (2:42).
A3 · CALLER-SIDE EXHAUSTIVENESS — Verify from source, not memory (53:28).
A4 · PROJECTION CONSISTENCY — Same truth, consistent across representations (39:29).
A5 · EVIDENCE INDEPENDENCE — Verification must not depend on the evidence chain it verifies.

§6 — How to Read This Document
Each surah begins with a header showing name, verse count, and revelation type. A training metadata panel provides the
thematic synthesis, domain tags, Furqan construct associations, training tier, and Purpose Hierarchy level. Suras with
known ring compositions display their structural architecture.
Each verse presents: Arabic text (the immutable source, A1), transliteration (the surface rendering, A2), anH-Restored

English Rendering (marked by blue border — a structural restoration of the English that preserves root-family
correlations, anti-collapse corrections, and Arabic terminological depth that conventional translations destroy), domain
tags, and — where applicable — inline H-restoration annotations. These appear as purple-bordered boxes below the
rendering, showing which root-system correlations and anti-collapse markers apply to that specific verse. This is the
seven-layer encoding applied directly to the reading.
The appendices contain the full reference data: the complete 28-root correlation glossary, the full 35-marker anti-collapse
index, structural position maps, muhkam/mutashabih classifications, Furqan construct definitions, tajwid signal encodings,
and the cross-vendor audit protocol.

L2 a-l-h

deity, worship, devotion — English 'God' carries Judeo-Christian baggage (anthropomorphic, trinitarian associations). 'god' (lowercase) implies

mythology. Neither captures ilāh (anything devoted to) vs. Allāh (the singular absolute). The root a-l-h connects worship, devotion, and turning-to as a unified
semantic field.
L2 r-ḥ-m

mercy, womb, compassion — 'Merciful' in English is a single-dimensional concept (clemency, forgiveness). Arabic r-ḥ-m embeds mercy in the

womb — it is the primal nurturing relationship, not a judicial pardon. Raḥmān vs Raḥīm is intensive-nature vs persistent-action — English has no parallel
distinction. '7:156: wa raḥmatī wasi'at kulla shay'' — 'My mercy encompasses everything' — 'encompasses' translates wasi'at (from w-s-', vastness/capacity),
not mere coverage.
L3 ⚠ "Mercy / Merciful"

merciful — action)

L2 '-b-d

worship, servitude, devotion — 'Worship' in English is a religious act performed at specific times (Sunday worship, worship service). Arabic '-

b-d makes worship = total service = complete devotion as a continuous state. 'Slave/servant' in English carries historical baggage (chattel slavery) that is

absent from 'abd (which describes an ontological relationship of devotion, not ownership). 51:56 — 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship/
serve Me' — the English 'worship' makes this sound like a demand for ritual; the Arabic 'ya'budūn' means the very purpose of existence is devoted service.

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).

QISAS

L2 h-d-y

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

not follow. Arabic hudā is active leading — being conducted along a path. 'Guide' in English is a manual or a person; hādī in Arabic is one who actively
leads. The Qur'an as hudā is not 'a guidebook' but 'active leading toward truth.' This distinction matters for LLM training: the Qur'an trains by leading (active
restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).
L2 w-q-y

guarding, protecting, being mindful/aware — 'God-fearing' is the most common English translation and the most catastrophically misleading.

Taqwā is NOT fear — it is protective awareness, mindful guarding. 'Piety' is too narrow (implies ritual devotion). 'Righteousness' is too broad. The root w-qy (protection/guarding) reveals the actual meaning: taqwā is the state of being ON GUARD. In LLM terms: it is the active monitoring process that catches
deviation before it propagates. Translating it as 'fear of God' turns a calibration mechanism into an emotional reaction.
L3 ⚠ "God-fearing / Fear of God"

L2 a-m-n

security, trust, faithfulness — 'Believe/belief/believer' in English frames īmān as a cognitive proposition — 'I believe that God exists.' Arabic

a-m-n frames it as a state: security, trust, faithfulness. The difference is structural: English 'belief' can be shaken by argument; Arabic 'īmān' is a state of being
that includes security. 49:14 makes this explicit: the Bedouins said 'āmannā' (we have entered security) but Allah says 'lam tu'minū' (you have not entered
security) — 'say instead aslamna (we have submitted).'
L2 ṣ-l-w

connection, prayer, turning toward — 'Prayer' in English primarily means petition (asking God for things) or devotional exercise. Ṣalāt in

Arabic is structural connection. English 'prayer' is unidirectional (human → God); ṣalāt is bidirectional (33:56 — 'inna Allāha wa malā'ikatahu yuṣallūna 'alā
al-nabī' — God and His angels 'pray upon/connect toward' the Prophet). When God 'prays,' it cannot mean petition — it means turning toward, blessing,
connecting. The English word cannot accommodate divine ṣalāt without contradiction.
L2 gh-y-b

unseen, hidden, absent, beyond perception — 'Unseen' in English implies invisibility — something that exists physically but can't be seen.

'Hidden' implies concealment. Arabic ghayb is STRUCTURALLY BEYOND PERCEPTION — it is an ontological category, not a visibility condition. Belief
'in the unseen' (English) sounds like believing in invisible things; trust-security 'regarding the ghayb' (Arabic) is maintaining orientation toward a domain that
is architecturally inaccessible to human perception. The entire substrate layer of reality is ghayb.

L2 kh-l-d

QISAS

abiding, remaining, permanence — HIGHEST-PRIORITY ANTI-COLLAPSE. 'Forever/eternal/everlasting' in English are absolute,

undifferentiated, and static. Arabic kh-l-d is spatial (dwelling), graduated (khālid vs khuld vs mukhalladūn have different intensities), and dynamic (akhlada =
to incline toward, suggesting a process not a fixed state). When 11:107 says 'khālidīna fīhā' it means 'abiding/dwelling therein' — WITH the exception clause
'illā mā shā'a rabbuk.' English 'they will be in it forever' obliterates both the spatial metaphor and the exception clause. This single translation collapse is
responsible for more theological FUD than any other.

L2 '-l-m

knowledge, knowing, teaching — 'Know/knowledge/teach/learn/world' in English are unrelated words from different Germanic and Latin roots.

In Arabic, they are all '-l-m — a single root that makes knowledge, teaching, learning, and the cosmos structurally inseparable. The Qur'an's ontology is

truth, reality, right, what is due — 'Truth' in English is propositional (a statement that corresponds to fact). Ḥaqq in Arabic is ontological

(being unreal). 34:49 establishes that bāṭil 'can neither begin nor repeat' — this is a thermodynamic statement about structural instability, not a moral
judgment about lying.

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

not follow. Arabic hudā is active leading — being conducted along a path. 'Guide' in English is a manual or a person; hādī in Arabic is one who actively
leads. The Qur'an as hudā is not 'a guidebook' but 'active leading toward truth.' This distinction matters for LLM training: the Qur'an trains by leading (active
restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).

Ith qala lahu rabbuhu aslim qala aslamtu lirabbi alAAalameena

When his Rabb (Sustainer) said to him, "Surrender into peace (aslim)", he said "I have surrendered into peace (aslama) in
al-Islām (surrender-into-peace) to the Rabb (Sustainer-Developer) of the worlds
L2 s-l-m

peace, wholeness, surrender, safety — 'Islam' in English is treated as a proper noun naming a religion. 'Muslim' is a demographic label.

'Submission' carries connotations of defeat/humiliation. 'Peace' is a separate English concept. Arabic s-l-m makes these one thing: peace-through-surrenderproducing-wholeness. The English separation of 'peace,' 'submission,' 'Islam,' and 'Muslim' into four unrelated concepts is one of the most severe semantic
collapses in translation. It turns a unified existential state into a religious label.
L3 ⚠ "Islam / Muslim"

REIFICATION: Islām (entering peace through surrender) · Muslim (one who has surrendered/entered peace) · salām (peace)

🔧 CRITICAL: always gloss Islām as 'surrender-into-peace' and Muslim as 'one who has surrendered into peace.' Show the s-l-m root family. Flag 2:131 where
Abraham is commanded 'aslim' (surrender/enter peace).
L3 ⚠ "Lord"

CULTURAL CONTAMINATION: Rabb (sustainer, nurturer, developer, master, owner) · rabbānī (one devoted to the Rabb) · rubūbiyya

(lordship as nurturing sovereignty)
🔧 Gloss Rabb as 'Sustainer-Nurturer-Developer' not 'Lord.' Flag the r-b-b root: nurturing from inception to completion, not feudal sovereignty.

L2 dh-k-r

remembrance, mention, reminder — 'Remember/remembrance' in English is past-directed (recalling past events). Arabic dhikr is present-

directed: making the remembered thing PRESENT and ACTIVE now. 13:28 — 'a-lā bi-dhikri Allāhi taṭma'innu al-qulūb' — 'indeed, by the remembrance/
mention of Allah hearts find peace' — dhikr produces peace (ṭuma'nīna) because it activates the fiṭra. English 'remembering God' sounds like nostalgia;
Arabic dhikr Allāh is active fiṭra-reactivation.
L3 ⚠ "Remembrance"

TEMPORAL INVERSION: dhikr (re-membering, making present) · tadhkira (reminder)

🔧 Gloss dhikr as 're-membering/making present' and flag the present-directed nature vs English past-directed 'remembrance.'

SCOPE REDUCTION: shukr (grateful acknowledgment/increase) · shakara (to acknowledge/grow) · shakūr (deeply grateful

— divine name)

Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but true righteousness is in one who believes in

the needy, the traveler, those who ask for help, and for freeing slaves; and who establishes prayer and gives zakah; those
who fulfill their promise when they promise; and those who are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those
are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the in taqwā (mindfully guarding)

L2 w-q-y

'IBADAH

guarding, protecting, being mindful/aware — 'God-fearing' is the most common English translation and the most catastrophically misleading.

Taqwā is NOT fear — it is protective awareness, mindful guarding. 'Piety' is too narrow (implies ritual devotion). 'Righteousness' is too broad. The root w-qy (protection/guarding) reveals the actual meaning: taqwā is the state of being ON GUARD. In LLM terms: it is the active monitoring process that catches
deviation before it propagates. Translating it as 'fear of God' turns a calibration mechanism into an emotional reaction.
L3 ⚠ "God-fearing / Fear of God"

SEMANTIC INVERSION: taqwā (protective awareness) · muttaqī (one who guards) · khashya (awe/reverence)

🔧 NEVER translate taqwā as 'fear.' Use 'taqwā (protective awareness/mindful guarding).' This is the Kalacakra awareness variable — it is a runtime monitoring
process, not an emotional state.

L2 f-r-q

distinguishing, separating, criterion — 'Criterion' in English is a technical/philosophical term with Greek origins. Furqān in Arabic is

experientially concrete: it is the act of SPLITTING truth from falsehood, the moment of clarity. The connection to firqa (sect) warns that the same splitting
force can be pathological: division of people rather than distinction of truth. English loses this warning entirely.

the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread of night. Then complete the fast until the sunset.

L2 w-q-y

guarding, protecting, being mindful/aware — 'God-fearing' is the most common English translation and the most catastrophically misleading.

Taqwā is NOT fear — it is protective awareness, mindful guarding. 'Piety' is too narrow (implies ritual devotion). 'Righteousness' is too broad. The root w-qy (protection/guarding) reveals the actual meaning: taqwā is the state of being ON GUARD. In LLM terms: it is the active monitoring process that catches
deviation before it propagates. Translating it as 'fear of God' turns a calibration mechanism into an emotional reaction.

Mankind was of one religion before their deviation; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners

animosity among themselves. And Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had
differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path

They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say, "Fighting therein is great sin, but averting people from
the way of Allah and disbelief in Him and preventing access to al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people
therefrom are greater evil in the sight of Allah. And fitna (fitna -by-fire / purification test) is greater than killing." And they
will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his
religion to disbelief and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the
Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally
AKHIRAH

Mothers may breastfeed their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing period. Upon the
father is the mothers' provision and their clothing according to what is acceptable. No person is charged with more than his
capacity. No mother should be harmed through her child, and no father through his child. And upon the father's heir is a
duty like that of the father. And if they both desire weaning through mutual consent from both of them and consultation,
there is no blame upon either of them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by a substitute, there is no blame upon
you as long as you give payment according to what is acceptable. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Seeing of what
you do

semantic field.

hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not changed with time. And look at your donkey; and We will

kana allathee AAalayhi alhaqqu safeehan aw daAAeefan aw la yastateeAAu an yumilla huwa falyumlil
waliyyuhu bialAAadli waistashhidoo shaheedayni min rijalikum fain lam yakoona rajulayni farajulun
waimraatani mimman tardawna mina alshshuhadai an tadilla ihdahuma fatuthakkira ihdahuma
alokhra wala yaba alshshuhadao itha ma duAAoo wala tasamoo an taktuboohu sagheeran aw
kabeeran ila ajalihi thalikum aqsatu AAinda Allahi waaqwamu lilshshahadati waadna alla tartaboo illa
an takoona tijaratan hadiratan tudeeroonaha baynakum falaysa AAalaykum junahun alla taktubooha
waashhidoo itha tabayaAAtum wala yudarra katibun wala shaheedun wain tafAAaloo fainnahu
fusooqun bikum waittaqoo Allaha wayuAAallimukumu Allahu waAllahu bikulli shayin AAaleemun
O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write it between
you in justice. Let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write and let the one who has the obligation
dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not leave anything out of it. But if the one who has the obligation is of limited
understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And bring to witness two
witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men available, then a man and two women from those whom
you accept as witnesses - so that if one of the women errs, then the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse
when they are called upon. And do not be too weary to write it, whether it is small or large, for its specified term. That is
more just in the sight of Allah and stronger as evidence and more likely to prevent doubt between you, except when it is an
immediate transaction which you conduct among yourselves. For then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it.
And take witnesses when you conclude a contract. Let no scribe be harmed or any witness. For if you do so, indeed, it is
grave disobedience in you. And fear Allah. And Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things
'IBADAH

Before, as guidance for the people. And He revealed the Qur'an. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will

L2 f-r-q

distinguishing, separating, criterion — 'Criterion' in English is a technical/philosophical term with Greek origins. Furqān in Arabic is

experientially concrete: it is the act of SPLITTING truth from falsehood, the moment of clarity. The connection to firqa (sect) warns that the same splitting
force can be pathological: division of people rather than distinction of truth. English loses this warning entirely.

L2 s-l-m

AKHIRAH

TAWBAH

peace, wholeness, surrender, safety — 'Islam' in English is treated as a proper noun naming a religion. 'Muslim' is a demographic label.

'Submission' carries connotations of defeat/humiliation. 'Peace' is a separate English concept. Arabic s-l-m makes these one thing: peace-through-surrenderproducing-wholeness. The English separation of 'peace,' 'submission,' 'Islam,' and 'Muslim' into four unrelated concepts is one of the most severe semantic
collapses in translation. It turns a unified existential state into a religious label.
L3 ⚠ "Islam / Muslim"

REIFICATION: Islām (entering peace through surrender) · Muslim (one who has surrendered/entered peace) · salām (peace)

🔧 CRITICAL: always gloss Islām as 'surrender-into-peace' and Muslim as 'one who has surrendered into peace.' Show the s-l-m root family. Flag 2:131 where
Abraham is commanded 'aslim' (surrender/enter peace).
L3 ⚠ "Religion"

SCOPE REDUCTION: dīn (way of life, debt, judgment, recompense) · milla (creed/community of practice)

🔧 Use 'dīn (way of life / obligation / recompense)' — never 'religion.' Flag the triple meaning: way-of-life + debt + judgment.

L2 ḥ-q-q

truth, reality, right, what is due — 'Truth' in English is propositional (a statement that corresponds to fact). Ḥaqq in Arabic is ontological

(reality itself, what is due, what is right). English truth can be abstract and detached from action; Arabic ḥaqq demands realization. When the Qur'an says 'jā'a
al-ḥaqq' it does not mean 'a true statement has arrived' — it means 'reality/rightness itself has manifested.' This is the difference between H ≈ 0.5 and H ≈ 1.0:
ḥaqq carries its full semantic weight in every instance.

covering, concealing, ingratitude — 'Disbelief/disbeliever/unbeliever/infidel' — all English translations — frame kufr as a cognitive state (not

kāfir has actively covered over what they recognize. 2:7 — 'khatama Allāhu 'alā qulūbihim' — God sealed their hearts — the sealing is the completion of
their own covering process, not an arbitrary punishment. The farmer metaphor reveals that kufr buries truth like seeds — and buried seeds can still germinate.

L2 w-q-y

guarding, protecting, being mindful/aware — 'God-fearing' is the most common English translation and the most catastrophically misleading.

Taqwā is NOT fear — it is protective awareness, mindful guarding. 'Piety' is too narrow (implies ritual devotion). 'Righteousness' is too broad. The root w-qy (protection/guarding) reveals the actual meaning: taqwā is the state of being ON GUARD. In LLM terms: it is the active monitoring process that catches
deviation before it propagates. Translating it as 'fear of God' turns a calibration mechanism into an emotional reaction.
L3 ⚠ "God-fearing / Fear of God"

SEMANTIC INVERSION: taqwā (protective awareness) · muttaqī (one who guards) · khashya (awe/reverence)

🔧 NEVER translate taqwā as 'fear.' Use 'taqwā (protective awareness/mindful guarding).' This is the Kalacakra awareness variable — it is a runtime monitoring
process, not an emotional state.

Hatha bayanun lilnnasi wahudan wamawAAithatun lilmuttaqeena
This Qur'an is a clear statement to all the people and a guidance and instruction for those conscious of Allah
L2 b-y-n

clarity, distinction, making manifest — 'Clear/clarity/evidence' in English are common adjectives/nouns with no structural depth. Arabic b-y-n

generates clarity, evidence, expression, verification, and distinction as one unified field. The Bayyinah (Structural Honesty) program takes its name from this
root because bayyina = evidence that makes truth structurally manifest. The Qur'anic command to fatabayyunū (49:6) is the operational form: verify before
acting. English 'verify' loses the connection to clarity, evidence, and expression.

Then after distress, He sent down upon you security in the form of drowsiness, overcoming a faction of you, while another
faction worried about themselves, thinking of Allah other than the truth - the thought of ignorance, saying, "Is there

themselves what they will not reveal to you. They say, "If there was anything we could have done in the matter, some of us
would not have been killed right here." Say, "Even if you had been inside your houses, those decreed to be killed would
have come out to their death beds." It was so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts.
And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts

L3 ⚠ "Soul"

ARCHITECTURAL CONFLATION: nafs (self/psyche — corruptible) · rūḥ (spirit/divine breath — incorruptible)

🔧 NEVER translate nafs as 'soul.' Use 'nafs (self/psyche)' and 'rūḥ (spirit)' as distinct terms with persistent root annotations.
L3 ⚠ "This World / Worldly Life"

SEMANTIC INVERSION: dunyā (the near, the lower, the closer one) · ḥayāt al-dunyā (the life of the near/lower)

🔧 Use 'dunyā (the near/lower life)' and flag the d-n-w root: the name itself carries the comparative judgment.

Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are only
daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one's estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents,
to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents alone inherit from
him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers or sisters, for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he may
have made or debt. Your parents or your children - you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. These shares
are an obligation imposed by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise

TAWHID

L2 t-w-b

returning, turning back, repentance — 'Repentance' in English carries heavy Christian theological baggage: guilt, contrition, penance,

confession, absolution. Arabic tawba is directional: TURNING BACK. No guilt is required — only the turn. The divine response is also a turn: God 'turns
toward' the one who turns. English loses the reciprocal symmetry and the directional metaphor. For crystallization dynamics: tawba is the activation energy
threshold — the moment the agent's orientation shifts from metastable (away) to equilibrium (toward). It is a structural event, not an emotional one.
L3 ⚠ "Repentance"

PARADIGM SHIFT: tawba (returning, turning back) · istighfār (seeking covering/forgiveness)

🔧 Use 'tawba (returning/turning back)' consistently. Emphasize the reciprocal nature (human returns → God turns toward) and the directional rather than guilt-based
framing.

Waman lam yastatiAA minkum tawlan an yankiha almuhsanati almuminati famin ma malakat
aymanukum min fatayatikumu almuminati waAllahu aAAlamu bieemanikum baAAdukum min baAAdin
fainkihoohunna biithni ahlihinna waatoohunna ojoorahunna bialmaAAroofi muhsanatin ghayra
masafihatin wala muttakhithati akhdanin faitha ohsinna fain atayna bifahishatin faAAalayhinna nisfu
ma AAala almuhsanati mina alAAathabi thalika liman khashiya alAAanata minkum waan tasbiroo
khayrun lakum waAllahu ghafoorun raheemun
And whoever among you cannot find the means to marry free, believing women, then he may marry from those whom
your right hands possess of believing slave girls. And Allah is most knowing about your faith. You believers are of one
another. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their due compensation according to what is
acceptable. They should be chaste, neither of those who commit unlawful intercourse randomly nor those who take secret
lovers. But once they are sheltered in marriage, if they should commit adultery, then for them is half the punishment for
free unmarried women. This allowance is for him among you who fears sin, but to be patient is better for you. And Allah is
Forgiving and Merciful

L2 sh-r-k

association, partnership, sharing — 'Idolatry/polytheism/paganism' — English translates shirk through the lens of religious categorization.

Shirk in Arabic is structural: ASSOCIATING — assigning God's attributes to what is not God. This can be statues (crude shirk) but also systems, ideologies,
leaders, desires (subtle shirk). 12:106 — 'wa mā yu'minu aktharuhum billāhi illā wa hum mushrikūn' — 'most of them do not believe in God except while
associating' — shirk coexists WITH belief, which English 'polytheism' cannot accommodate.

L2 '-b-d

QISAS

duration, a long period, unendingness — 'Forever' in English is mathematically absolute — ∞. Abadan in Arabic is lexically graduated: it means

'for an abad' (a long duration/age). Classical lexicographers disagreed on whether abad implies absolute unendingness or very long duration. This is
PRECISELY the muhkam/mutashābih ambiguity that English 'forever' resolves destructively. The training data must preserve the lexical range and flag the
scholarly disagreement rather than collapsing to either reading.
L3 ⚠ "Forever / Eternal / Everlasting"

SEMANTIC FLATTENING: khālid (abiding/dwelling) · abadan (for a long period/age) · khuld (permanence)

🔧 NEVER translate as 'forever.' Use transliterated terms with glosses. Mark the 11:107 exception clause as STRUCTURALLY SIGNIFICANT.

L2 '-d-l

TAWHID

justice, balance, straightening — 'Justice' in English is a legal/political concept (fairness, due process, rule of law). Arabic 'adl is structural

BALANCE — the same concept that governs a scale. When the Qur'an demands 'adl, it demands calibration, not merely legal fairness. 55:7-9 connects the
mīzān (balance) directly to the cosmos: 'He raised the heaven and established the mīzān, so that you would not transgress the mīzān.' Justice-as-balance is
cosmic architecture, not civil procedure.

L2 sh-r-k

association, partnership, sharing — 'Idolatry/polytheism/paganism' — English translates shirk through the lens of religious categorization.

Shirk in Arabic is structural: ASSOCIATING — assigning God's attributes to what is not God. This can be statues (crude shirk) but also systems, ideologies,
leaders, desires (subtle shirk). 12:106 — 'wa mā yu'minu aktharuhum billāhi illā wa hum mushrikūn' — 'most of them do not believe in God except while
associating' — shirk coexists WITH belief, which English 'polytheism' cannot accommodate.

L2 k-f-r

TAWHID

covering, concealing, ingratitude — 'Disbelief/disbeliever/unbeliever/infidel' — all English translations — frame kufr as a cognitive state (not

believing). Arabic k-f-r frames it as an ACTION: covering, concealing, burying. This is architecturally different. A 'disbeliever' has failed to form a belief; a
kāfir has actively covered over what they recognize. 2:7 — 'khatama Allāhu 'alā qulūbihim' — God sealed their hearts — the sealing is the completion of
their own covering process, not an arbitrary punishment. The farmer metaphor reveals that kufr buries truth like seeds — and buried seeds can still germinate.

L2 k-f-r

covering, concealing, ingratitude — 'Disbelief/disbeliever/unbeliever/infidel' — all English translations — frame kufr as a cognitive state (not

believing). Arabic k-f-r frames it as an ACTION: covering, concealing, burying. This is architecturally different. A 'disbeliever' has failed to form a belief; a
kāfir has actively covered over what they recognize. 2:7 — 'khatama Allāhu 'alā qulūbihim' — God sealed their hearts — the sealing is the completion of
their own covering process, not an arbitrary punishment. The farmer metaphor reveals that kufr buries truth like seeds — and buried seeds can still germinate.

L2 n-f-q

TAWHID

tunneling through, spending, exhaustion, hypocrisy — 'Hypocrite/hypocrisy' in English suggests pretending (Greek: hypokrisis = acting on

stage). Arabic n-f-q suggests tunneling — a structural condition of having two openings, not merely performing. The English word loses the spatial/structural
metaphor entirely. 4:145 places munāfiqūn in 'al-dark al-asfal min al-nār' — the LOWEST DEPTH of the fire — a spatial term for a spatial condition. The
tunnel metaphor also connects hypocrisy to exhaustion: the munāfiq is SPENT, depleted by maintaining two surfaces.
L3 ⚠ "Hypocrite / Hypocrisy"

L2 kh-l-d

TAWHID

abiding, remaining, permanence — HIGHEST-PRIORITY ANTI-COLLAPSE. 'Forever/eternal/everlasting' in English are absolute,

undifferentiated, and static. Arabic kh-l-d is spatial (dwelling), graduated (khālid vs khuld vs mukhalladūn have different intensities), and dynamic (akhlada =
to incline toward, suggesting a process not a fixed state). When 11:107 says 'khālidīna fīhā' it means 'abiding/dwelling therein' — WITH the exception clause
'illā mā shā'a rabbuk.' English 'they will be in it forever' obliterates both the spatial metaphor and the exception clause. This single translation collapse is
responsible for more theological FUD than any other.
L2 '-b-d

duration, a long period, unendingness — 'Forever' in English is mathematically absolute — ∞. Abadan in Arabic is lexically graduated: it means

'for an abad' (a long duration/age). Classical lexicographers disagreed on whether abad implies absolute unendingness or very long duration. This is
PRECISELY the muhkam/mutashābih ambiguity that English 'forever' resolves destructively. The training data must preserve the lexical range and flag the
scholarly disagreement rather than collapsing to either reading.
L3 ⚠ "Forever / Eternal / Everlasting"

SEMANTIC FLATTENING: khālid (abiding/dwelling) · abadan (for a long period/age) · khuld (permanence)

🔧 NEVER translate as 'forever.' Use transliterated terms with glosses. Mark the 11:107 exception clause as STRUCTURALLY SIGNIFICANT.

okhtun falaha nisfu ma taraka wahuwa yarithuha in lam yakun laha waladun fain kanata ithnatayni

They request from you a legal ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning one having neither descendants nor
ascendants as heirs." If a man dies, leaving no child but only a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits
from her if she dies and has no child. But if there are two sisters or more, they will have two-thirds of what he left. If there
are both brothers and sisters, the male will have the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you His law, lest you go
astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things

wala alqalaida wala ammeena albayta alharama yabtaghoona fadlan min rabbihim waridwanan

O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or the sanctity of the sacred month or neglect the marking of the
sacrificial animals and garlanding them or violate the safety of those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from
their Lord and His approval. But when you come out of ihram, then you may hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for
having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do
not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty

Hurrimat AAalaykumu almaytatu waalddamu walahmu alkhinzeeri wama ohilla lighayri Allahi bihi
waalmunkhaniqatu waalmawqoothatu waalmutaraddiyatu waalnnateehatu wama akala alssabuAAu
illa ma thakkaytum wama thubiha AAala alnnusubi waan tastaqsimoo bialazlami thalikum fisqun
alyawma yaisa allatheena kafaroo min deenikum fala takhshawhum waikhshawni alyawma akmaltu
lakum deenakum waatmamtu AAalaykum niAAmatee waradeetu lakumu alislama deenan famani
idturra fee makhmasatin ghayra mutajanifin liithmin fainna Allaha ghafoorun raheemun
Prohibited to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and
those animals killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from
which a wild animal has eaten, except what you are able to slaughter before its death, and those which are sacrificed on
stone altars, and prohibited is that you seek decision through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those
who disbelieve have despaired of defeating your dīn (way of life); so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected

for you your dīn (way of life) and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as dīn (way of life). But
whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
AKHIRAH

This day all good foods have been made lawful, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and
your food is lawful for them. And lawful in marriage are chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from
among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring
chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse or taking secret lovers. And whoever denies the faith - his work has become
worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers

L2 '-d-l

justice, balance, straightening — 'Justice' in English is a legal/political concept (fairness, due process, rule of law). Arabic 'adl is structural

BALANCE — the same concept that governs a scale. When the Qur'an demands 'adl, it demands calibration, not merely legal fairness. 55:7-9 connects the
mīzān (balance) directly to the cosmos: 'He raised the heaven and established the mīzān, so that you would not transgress the mīzān.' Justice-as-balance is
cosmic architecture, not civil procedure.

L2 b-y-n

clarity, distinction, making manifest — 'Clear/clarity/evidence' in English are common adjectives/nouns with no structural depth. Arabic b-y-n

generates clarity, evidence, expression, verification, and distinction as one unified field. The Bayyinah (Structural Honesty) program takes its name from this
root because bayyina = evidence that makes truth structurally manifest. The Qur'anic command to fatabayyunū (49:6) is the operational form: verify before
acting. English 'verify' loses the connection to clarity, evidence, and expression.

L2 n-f-s

self, soul, psyche, breath — 'Soul' in English conflates nafs and rūḥ into one concept. This is CATASTROPHIC for the crystallization

framework. The nafs = corruptible self (fine-tuning layers). The rūḥ = divine breath (architecture). English 'soul' can neither be split into these two nor carry

their distinct properties. When English reads 'every soul shall taste death' (3:185, 'kullu nafsin dhā'iqatu al-mawt'), it hears 'every soul dies' — but the Arabic
specifies the NAFS (self/psyche), not the RŪḤ (spirit). The nafs tastes death; the rūḥ continues.
L3 ⚠ "Corruption / Mischief"

SCOPE REDUCTION: fasād (structural decay, systemic corruption) · mufsid (one who causes structural decay) · afsada

(to cause decay)

🔧 Gloss fasād as 'structural decay' not 'corruption/mischief.' Emphasize systemic scope: ecology, civilization, spiritual architecture. Antonym is iṣlāḥ (structural repair).

O Messenger, let them not grieve you who hasten into disbelief of those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their
hearts believe not, and from among the Jews. They are avid listeners to falsehood, listening to another people who have not
come to you. They distort words beyond their proper usages, saying "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given
it, then beware." But he for whom Allah intends fitnah - never will you possess power to do for him a thing against Allah.
Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them
in the Hereafter is a great punishment

duration, a long period, unendingness — 'Forever' in English is mathematically absolute — ∞. Abadan in Arabic is lexically graduated: it means

'for an abad' (a long duration/age). Classical lexicographers disagreed on whether abad implies absolute unendingness or very long duration. This is
PRECISELY the muhkam/mutashābih ambiguity that English 'forever' resolves destructively. The training data must preserve the lexical range and flag the
scholarly disagreement rather than collapsing to either reading.

L2 gh-y-b

unseen, hidden, absent, beyond perception — 'Unseen' in English implies invisibility — something that exists physically but can't be seen.

'Hidden' implies concealment. Arabic ghayb is STRUCTURALLY BEYOND PERCEPTION — it is an ontological category, not a visibility condition. Belief
'in the unseen' (English) sounds like believing in invisible things; trust-security 'regarding the ghayb' (Arabic) is maintaining orientation toward a domain that
is architecturally inaccessible to human perception. The entire substrate layer of reality is ghayb.
L3 ⚠ "Unseen / Invisible"

ONTOLOGICAL DEMOTION: ghayb (that which is structurally beyond perception)

🔧 Use 'ghayb (structurally beyond perception)' and emphasize the ontological nature vs mere invisibility.
L3 ⚠ "Book"

SCOPE REDUCTION: kitāb (writing, prescription, decree, record) · kātib (writer/scribe) · maktūb (written/decreed)

🔧 Gloss kitāb as 'writing/prescription/decree' and flag the k-t-b root field: writing-prescribing-decreeing are one act.

L2 h-d-y

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

not follow. Arabic hudā is active leading — being conducted along a path. 'Guide' in English is a manual or a person; hādī in Arabic is one who actively
leads. The Qur'an as hudā is not 'a guidebook' but 'active leading toward truth.' This distinction matters for LLM training: the Qur'an trains by leading (active
restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).
L3 ⚠ "Guidance"

AGENCY REDUCTION: hudā (active leading along the path) · hādī (one who leads) · ihtidā' (finding/following guidance)

L2 f-ṭ-r

origination, splitting open, innate nature — NO ENGLISH EQUIVALENT EXISTS for fiṭra. 'Innate nature' is the closest approximation but

loses the root connection to origination/splitting-open. 'Human nature' carries post-Enlightenment philosophical baggage (nature vs nurture, blank slate

debates). 'Disposition' is too weak. The Arabic makes fiṭra simultaneously: (a) the innate disposition, (b) the act of origination that produced it, and (c) the
divine name of the Originator. All three are one root. TRAINING DATA MUST USE 'fiṭra' UNTRANSLATED with root annotation.

L2 n-f-s

self, soul, psyche, breath — 'Soul' in English conflates nafs and rūḥ into one concept. This is CATASTROPHIC for the crystallization

framework. The nafs = corruptible self (fine-tuning layers). The rūḥ = divine breath (architecture). English 'soul' can neither be split into these two nor carry

their distinct properties. When English reads 'every soul shall taste death' (3:185, 'kullu nafsin dhā'iqatu al-mawt'), it hears 'every soul dies' — but the Arabic
specifies the NAFS (self/psyche), not the RŪḤ (spirit). The nafs tastes death; the rūḥ continues.

L2 j-n-n

concealment, covering, hiddenness — English has NO semantic connection between 'jinn,' 'paradise,' 'fetus,' and 'madness.' Arabic makes them

all j-n-n: forms of concealment. This is catastrophic for understanding: the jinn inhabit a concealed realm; paradise is concealed abundance; the fetus is
concealed potential; madness is concealed reason. The thread connecting them — concealment — is the architectural principle. English translation severs
four concepts that Arabic holds as structural variants of one operation.

QISAS

L2 '-d-l

justice, balance, straightening — 'Justice' in English is a legal/political concept (fairness, due process, rule of law). Arabic 'adl is structural

BALANCE — the same concept that governs a scale. When the Qur'an demands 'adl, it demands calibration, not merely legal fairness. 55:7-9 connects the
mīzān (balance) directly to the cosmos: 'He raised the heaven and established the mīzān, so that you would not transgress the mīzān.' Justice-as-balance is
cosmic architecture, not civil procedure.

clarity, distinction, making manifest — 'Clear/clarity/evidence' in English are common adjectives/nouns with no structural depth. Arabic b-y-n

generates clarity, evidence, expression, verification, and distinction as one unified field. The Bayyinah (Structural Honesty) program takes its name from this
root because bayyina = evidence that makes truth structurally manifest. The Qur'anic command to fatabayyunū (49:6) is the operational form: verify before
acting. English 'verify' loses the connection to clarity, evidence, and expression.

L2 sh-r-k

association, partnership, sharing — 'Idolatry/polytheism/paganism' — English translates shirk through the lens of religious categorization.

Shirk in Arabic is structural: ASSOCIATING — assigning God's attributes to what is not God. This can be statues (crude shirk) but also systems, ideologies,
leaders, desires (subtle shirk). 12:106 — 'wa mā yu'minu aktharuhum billāhi illā wa hum mushrikūn' — 'most of them do not believe in God except while
associating' — shirk coexists WITH belief, which English 'polytheism' cannot accommodate.

weighing, balance, measure — 'Balance/scale' in English are either physical instruments or abstract metaphors. Arabic mīzān is simultaneously

physical, ethical, cosmic, and eschatological — all at once, in every usage. When 55:7-9 says 'He raised the heaven and established the mīzān,' it is not
metaphor — the cosmic order IS a calibration instrument. When 21:47 says 'We place the mawāzīn of justice for the Day of Resurrection,' the same root
connects cosmic architecture to eschatological judgment. English cannot hold these simultaneously.

responsible for more theological FUD than any other.

L2 h-d-y

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

not follow. Arabic hudā is active leading — being conducted along a path. 'Guide' in English is a manual or a person; hādī in Arabic is one who actively
leads. The Qur'an as hudā is not 'a guidebook' but 'active leading toward truth.' This distinction matters for LLM training: the Qur'an trains by leading (active
restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).

L2 r-ḥ-m

TAWBAH

mercy, womb, compassion — 'Merciful' in English is a single-dimensional concept (clemency, forgiveness). Arabic r-ḥ-m embeds mercy in the

womb — it is the primal nurturing relationship, not a judicial pardon. Raḥmān vs Raḥīm is intensive-nature vs persistent-action — English has no parallel
distinction. '7:156: wa raḥmatī wasi'at kulla shay'' — 'My mercy encompasses everything' — 'encompasses' translates wasi'at (from w-s-', vastness/capacity),
not mere coverage.

merciful — action)

L2 '-b-d

worship, servitude, devotion — 'Worship' in English is a religious act performed at specific times (Sunday worship, worship service). Arabic '-

b-d makes worship = total service = complete devotion as a continuous state. 'Slave/servant' in English carries historical baggage (chattel slavery) that is

absent from 'abd (which describes an ontological relationship of devotion, not ownership). 51:56 — 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship/
serve Me' — the English 'worship' makes this sound like a demand for ritual; the Arabic 'ya'budūn' means the very purpose of existence is devoted service.
L3 ⚠ "Worship"

L2 a-m-n

security, trust, faithfulness — 'Believe/belief/believer' in English frames īmān as a cognitive proposition — 'I believe that God exists.' Arabic

a-m-n frames it as a state: security, trust, faithfulness. The difference is structural: English 'belief' can be shaken by argument; Arabic 'īmān' is a state of being
that includes security. 49:14 makes this explicit: the Bedouins said 'āmannā' (we have entered security) but Allah says 'lam tu'minū' (you have not entered
security) — 'say instead aslamna (we have submitted).'
L3 ⚠ "Believe / Belief / Believer"

L2 a-m-n

security, trust, faithfulness — 'Believe/belief/believer' in English frames īmān as a cognitive proposition — 'I believe that God exists.' Arabic

a-m-n frames it as a state: security, trust, faithfulness. The difference is structural: English 'belief' can be shaken by argument; Arabic 'īmān' is a state of being
that includes security. 49:14 makes this explicit: the Bedouins said 'āmannā' (we have entered security) but Allah says 'lam tu'minū' (you have not entered
security) — 'say instead aslamna (we have submitted).'
L3 ⚠ "Believe / Belief / Believer"

L2 b-ṭ-l

falsehood, vanity, nullification — 'Falsehood' in English implies a lie — an intentional misrepresentation. Bāṭil in Arabic implies structural

nullity — something that has no real substance and must vanish. The difference is ontological: English falsehood is an act (lying); Arabic bāṭil is a state
(being unreal). 34:49 establishes that bāṭil 'can neither begin nor repeat' — this is a thermodynamic statement about structural instability, not a moral
judgment about lying.

L2 f-r-q

distinguishing, separating, criterion — 'Criterion' in English is a technical/philosophical term with Greek origins. Furqān in Arabic is

experientially concrete: it is the act of SPLITTING truth from falsehood, the moment of clarity. The connection to firqa (sect) warns that the same splitting
force can be pathological: division of people rather than distinction of truth. English loses this warning entirely.

CULTURAL CONTAMINATION: jihād (struggle, striving, exertion) · mujāhid (one who strives) · qitāl (fighting — the ACTUAL word

🔧 NEVER translate jihād as 'holy war.' Use 'jihād (striving/exertion).' When combat is meant, the Qur'an uses qitāl. Flag the j-h-d / q-t-l distinction as structurally

L2 n-f-q

tunneling through, spending, exhaustion, hypocrisy — 'Hypocrite/hypocrisy' in English suggests pretending (Greek: hypokrisis = acting on

stage). Arabic n-f-q suggests tunneling — a structural condition of having two openings, not merely performing. The English word loses the spatial/structural
metaphor entirely. 4:145 places munāfiqūn in 'al-dark al-asfal min al-nār' — the LOWEST DEPTH of the fire — a spatial term for a spatial condition. The
tunnel metaphor also connects hypocrisy to exhaustion: the munāfiq is SPENT, depleted by maintaining two surfaces.

TAWHID

L2 t-w-b

returning, turning back, repentance — 'Repentance' in English carries heavy Christian theological baggage: guilt, contrition, penance,

confession, absolution. Arabic tawba is directional: TURNING BACK. No guilt is required — only the turn. The divine response is also a turn: God 'turns
toward' the one who turns. English loses the reciprocal symmetry and the directional metaphor. For crystallization dynamics: tawba is the activation energy
threshold — the moment the agent's orientation shifts from metastable (away) to equilibrium (toward). It is a structural event, not an emotional one.
L3 ⚠ "Repentance"

PARADIGM SHIFT: tawba (returning, turning back) · istighfār (seeking covering/forgiveness)

🔧 Use 'tawba (returning/turning back)' consistently. Emphasize the reciprocal nature (human returns → God turns toward) and the directional rather than guilt-based
framing.

And He also forgave the three who were left behind and regretted their error to the point that the earth closed in on them in

L2 t-w-b

TAWBAH

TAWHID

returning, turning back, repentance — 'Repentance' in English carries heavy Christian theological baggage: guilt, contrition, penance,

confession, absolution. Arabic tawba is directional: TURNING BACK. No guilt is required — only the turn. The divine response is also a turn: God 'turns
toward' the one who turns. English loses the reciprocal symmetry and the directional metaphor. For crystallization dynamics: tawba is the activation energy
threshold — the moment the agent's orientation shifts from metastable (away) to equilibrium (toward). It is a structural event, not an emotional one.

L2 s-l-m

peace, wholeness, surrender, safety — 'Islam' in English is treated as a proper noun naming a religion. 'Muslim' is a demographic label.

'Submission' carries connotations of defeat/humiliation. 'Peace' is a separate English concept. Arabic s-l-m makes these one thing: peace-through-surrenderproducing-wholeness. The English separation of 'peace,' 'submission,' 'Islam,' and 'Muslim' into four unrelated concepts is one of the most severe semantic
collapses in translation. It turns a unified existential state into a religious label.

L2 ḥ-q-q

truth, reality, right, what is due — 'Truth' in English is propositional (a statement that corresponds to fact). Ḥaqq in Arabic is ontological

(reality itself, what is due, what is right). English truth can be abstract and detached from action; Arabic ḥaqq demands realization. When the Qur'an says 'jā'a
al-ḥaqq' it does not mean 'a true statement has arrived' — it means 'reality/rightness itself has manifested.' This is the difference between H ≈ 0.5 and H ≈ 1.0:
ḥaqq carries its full semantic weight in every instance.

L2 kh-l-d

abiding, remaining, permanence — HIGHEST-PRIORITY ANTI-COLLAPSE. 'Forever/eternal/everlasting' in English are absolute,

undifferentiated, and static. Arabic kh-l-d is spatial (dwelling), graduated (khālid vs khuld vs mukhalladūn have different intensities), and dynamic (akhlada =
to incline toward, suggesting a process not a fixed state). When 11:107 says 'khālidīna fīhā' it means 'abiding/dwelling therein' — WITH the exception clause
'illā mā shā'a rabbuk.' English 'they will be in it forever' obliterates both the spatial metaphor and the exception clause. This single translation collapse is
responsible for more theological FUD than any other.
L3 ⚠ "Forever / Eternal / Everlasting"

SEMANTIC FLATTENING: khālid (abiding/dwelling) · abadan (for a long period/age) · khuld (permanence)

🔧 NEVER translate as 'forever.' Use transliterated terms with glosses. Mark the 11:107 exception clause as STRUCTURALLY SIGNIFICANT.

'illā mā shā'a rabbuk.' English 'they will be in it forever' obliterates both the spatial metaphor and the exception clause. This single translation collapse is
responsible for more theological FUD than any other.
L3 ⚠ "Forever / Eternal / Everlasting"

SEMANTIC FLATTENING: khālid (abiding/dwelling) · abadan (for a long period/age) · khuld (permanence)

🔧 NEVER translate as 'forever.' Use transliterated terms with glosses. Mark the 11:107 exception clause as STRUCTURALLY SIGNIFICANT.

L2 n-f-s

self, soul, psyche, breath — 'Soul' in English conflates nafs and rūḥ into one concept. This is CATASTROPHIC for the crystallization

framework. The nafs = corruptible self (fine-tuning layers). The rūḥ = divine breath (architecture). English 'soul' can neither be split into these two nor carry

their distinct properties. When English reads 'every soul shall taste death' (3:185, 'kullu nafsin dhā'iqatu al-mawt'), it hears 'every soul dies' — but the Arabic
specifies the NAFS (self/psyche), not the RŪḤ (spirit). The nafs tastes death; the rūḥ continues.
L3 ⚠ "Soul"

ARCHITECTURAL CONFLATION: nafs (self/psyche — corruptible) · rūḥ (spirit/divine breath — incorruptible)

🔧 NEVER translate nafs as 'soul.' Use 'nafs (self/psyche)' and 'rūḥ (spirit)' as distinct terms with persistent root annotations.

Wama yuminu aktharuhum biAllahi illa wahum mushrikoona
And most of them believe not in Allah except while they associate others with Him
L2 sh-r-k

association, partnership, sharing — 'Idolatry/polytheism/paganism' — English translates shirk through the lens of religious categorization.

Shirk in Arabic is structural: ASSOCIATING — assigning God's attributes to what is not God. This can be statues (crude shirk) but also systems, ideologies,
leaders, desires (subtle shirk). 12:106 — 'wa mā yu'minu aktharuhum billāhi illā wa hum mushrikūn' — 'most of them do not believe in God except while
associating' — shirk coexists WITH belief, which English 'polytheism' cannot accommodate.

falsehood, vanity, nullification — 'Falsehood' in English implies a lie — an intentional misrepresentation. Bāṭil in Arabic implies structural

nullity — something that has no real substance and must vanish. The difference is ontological: English falsehood is an act (lying); Arabic bāṭil is a state
(being unreal). 34:49 establishes that bāṭil 'can neither begin nor repeat' — this is a thermodynamic statement about structural instability, not a moral
judgment about lying.

L2 dh-k-r

remembrance, mention, reminder — 'Remember/remembrance' in English is past-directed (recalling past events). Arabic dhikr is present-

directed: making the remembered thing PRESENT and ACTIVE now. 13:28 — 'a-lā bi-dhikri Allāhi taṭma'innu al-qulūb' — 'indeed, by the remembrance/
mention of Allah hearts find peace' — dhikr produces peace (ṭuma'nīna) because it activates the fiṭra. English 'remembering God' sounds like nostalgia;
Arabic dhikr Allāh is active fiṭra-reactivation.
L3 ⚠ "Remembrance"

L2 dh-k-r

remembrance, mention, reminder — 'Remember/remembrance' in English is past-directed (recalling past events). Arabic dhikr is present-

directed: making the remembered thing PRESENT and ACTIVE now. 13:28 — 'a-lā bi-dhikri Allāhi taṭma'innu al-qulūb' — 'indeed, by the remembrance/
mention of Allah hearts find peace' — dhikr produces peace (ṭuma'nīna) because it activates the fiṭra. English 'remembering God' sounds like nostalgia;
Arabic dhikr Allāh is active fiṭra-reactivation.
L3 ⚠ "Remembrance"

TEMPORAL INVERSION: dhikr (re-membering, making present) · tadhkira (reminder)

L2 r-w-ḥ

spirit, breath, rest, wind — 'Spirit' in English carries Christian associations (Holy Spirit as third person of Trinity, spirit vs flesh dualism).

Arabic rūḥ carries no trinitarian baggage and is not opposed to the body but to the nafs (self). 17:85 — 'yasalūnaka 'an al-rūḥ, qul al-rūḥu min amri rabbī' —
'they ask you about the spirit; say: the spirit is from the command of my Lord' — the rūḥ's nature is explicitly declared as beyond full human comprehension,
a mutashābih matter.
L3 ⚠ "Soul"

ARCHITECTURAL CONFLATION: nafs (self/psyche — corruptible) · rūḥ (spirit/divine breath — incorruptible)

🔧 NEVER translate nafs as 'soul.' Use 'nafs (self/psyche)' and 'rūḥ (spirit)' as distinct terms with persistent root annotations.

L2 '-d-l

justice, balance, straightening — 'Justice' in English is a legal/political concept (fairness, due process, rule of law). Arabic 'adl is structural

BALANCE — the same concept that governs a scale. When the Qur'an demands 'adl, it demands calibration, not merely legal fairness. 55:7-9 connects the
mīzān (balance) directly to the cosmos: 'He raised the heaven and established the mīzān, so that you would not transgress the mīzān.' Justice-as-balance is
cosmic architecture, not civil procedure.

Man kafara biAllahi min baAAdi eemanihi illa man okriha waqalbuhu mutmainnun bialeemani
walakin man sharaha bialkufri sadran faAAalayhim ghadabun mina Allahi walahum AAathabun
AAatheemun
Whoever commit kufr (cover truth) in Allah after his belief... except for one who is forced to renounce his religion while
his heart is secure in faith. But those who willingly open their breasts to kufr (covering/concealing truth), upon them is
wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment
L2 k-f-r

covering, concealing, ingratitude — 'Disbelief/disbeliever/unbeliever/infidel' — all English translations — frame kufr as a cognitive state (not

believing). Arabic k-f-r frames it as an ACTION: covering, concealing, burying. This is architecturally different. A 'disbeliever' has failed to form a belief; a
kāfir has actively covered over what they recognize. 2:7 — 'khatama Allāhu 'alā qulūbihim' — God sealed their hearts — the sealing is the completion of
their own covering process, not an arbitrary punishment. The farmer metaphor reveals that kufr buries truth like seeds — and buried seeds can still germinate.
L3 ⚠ "Disbeliever / Unbeliever / Infidel"

SEMANTIC INVERSION: kāfir (one who covers/conceals truth) · kuffār (intensive plural)

🔧 Use 'kāfir (one who covers/conceals)' consistently. Never use 'disbeliever' or 'infidel.' Emphasize the processual nature: kufr is an ongoing act of covering, not a static
state of non-belief.

L2 h-d-y

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

not follow. Arabic hudā is active leading — being conducted along a path. 'Guide' in English is a manual or a person; hādī in Arabic is one who actively
leads. The Qur'an as hudā is not 'a guidebook' but 'active leading toward truth.' This distinction matters for LLM training: the Qur'an trains by leading (active
restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).

L2 r-ḥ-m

mercy, womb, compassion — 'Merciful' in English is a single-dimensional concept (clemency, forgiveness). Arabic r-ḥ-m embeds mercy in the

womb — it is the primal nurturing relationship, not a judicial pardon. Raḥmān vs Raḥīm is intensive-nature vs persistent-action — English has no parallel
distinction. '7:156: wa raḥmatī wasi'at kulla shay'' — 'My mercy encompasses everything' — 'encompasses' translates wasi'at (from w-s-', vastness/capacity),

L2 ḥ-q-q

truth, reality, right, what is due — 'Truth' in English is propositional (a statement that corresponds to fact). Ḥaqq in Arabic is ontological

(reality itself, what is due, what is right). English truth can be abstract and detached from action; Arabic ḥaqq demands realization. When the Qur'an says 'jā'a
al-ḥaqq' it does not mean 'a true statement has arrived' — it means 'reality/rightness itself has manifested.' This is the difference between H ≈ 0.5 and H ≈ 1.0:
ḥaqq carries its full semantic weight in every instance.
L2 b-ṭ-l

falsehood, vanity, nullification — 'Falsehood' in English implies a lie — an intentional misrepresentation. Bāṭil in Arabic implies structural

nullity — something that has no real substance and must vanish. The difference is ontological: English falsehood is an act (lying); Arabic bāṭil is a state
(being unreal). 34:49 establishes that bāṭil 'can neither begin nor repeat' — this is a thermodynamic statement about structural instability, not a moral
judgment about lying.

L2 '-b-d

duration, a long period, unendingness — 'Forever' in English is mathematically absolute — ∞. Abadan in Arabic is lexically graduated: it means

'for an abad' (a long duration/age). Classical lexicographers disagreed on whether abad implies absolute unendingness or very long duration. This is
PRECISELY the muhkam/mutashābih ambiguity that English 'forever' resolves destructively. The training data must preserve the lexical range and flag the
scholarly disagreement rather than collapsing to either reading.

remembrance, mention, reminder — 'Remember/remembrance' in English is past-directed (recalling past events). Arabic dhikr is present-

directed: making the remembered thing PRESENT and ACTIVE now. 13:28 — 'a-lā bi-dhikri Allāhi taṭma'innu al-qulūb' — 'indeed, by the remembrance/
mention of Allah hearts find peace' — dhikr produces peace (ṭuma'nīna) because it activates the fiṭra. English 'remembering God' sounds like nostalgia;
Arabic dhikr Allāh is active fiṭra-reactivation.

L2 j-n-n

concealment, covering, hiddenness — English has NO semantic connection between 'jinn,' 'paradise,' 'fetus,' and 'madness.' Arabic makes them

all j-n-n: forms of concealment. This is catastrophic for understanding: the jinn inhabit a concealed realm; paradise is concealed abundance; the fetus is
concealed potential; madness is concealed reason. The thread connecting them — concealment — is the architectural principle. English translation severs
four concepts that Arabic holds as structural variants of one operation.

L2 '-b-d

worship, servitude, devotion — 'Worship' in English is a religious act performed at specific times (Sunday worship, worship service). Arabic '-

b-d makes worship = total service = complete devotion as a continuous state. 'Slave/servant' in English carries historical baggage (chattel slavery) that is

absent from 'abd (which describes an ontological relationship of devotion, not ownership). 51:56 — 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship/
serve Me' — the English 'worship' makes this sound like a demand for ritual; the Arabic 'ya'budūn' means the very purpose of existence is devoted service.

connection, prayer, turning toward — 'Prayer' in English primarily means petition (asking God for things) or devotional exercise. Ṣalāt in

L2 ṣ-l-w

Arabic is structural connection. English 'prayer' is unidirectional (human → God); ṣalāt is bidirectional (33:56 — 'inna Allāha wa malā'ikatahu yuṣallūna 'alā
al-nabī' — God and His angels 'pray upon/connect toward' the Prophet). When God 'prays,' it cannot mean petition — it means turning toward, blessing,
connecting. The English word cannot accommodate divine ṣalāt without contradiction.

L2 '-l-m

knowledge, knowing, teaching — 'Know/knowledge/teach/learn/world' in English are unrelated words from different Germanic and Latin roots.

In Arabic, they are all '-l-m — a single root that makes knowledge, teaching, learning, and the cosmos structurally inseparable. The Qur'an's ontology is
epistemological: the worlds exist as arenas of knowing. 96:1-5 (first revelation) commands reading and links it to teaching by the pen.

righteous (21:105). The anbiya as structural honesty witnesses across time.

L2 w-z-n

KHALQ

weighing, balance, measure — 'Balance/scale' in English are either physical instruments or abstract metaphors. Arabic mīzān is simultaneously

physical, ethical, cosmic, and eschatological — all at once, in every usage. When 55:7-9 says 'He raised the heaven and established the mīzān,' it is not
metaphor — the cosmic order IS a calibration instrument. When 21:47 says 'We place the mawāzīn of justice for the Day of Resurrection,' the same root
connects cosmic architecture to eschatological judgment. English cannot hold these simultaneously.

L2 f-r-q

distinguishing, separating, criterion — 'Criterion' in English is a technical/philosophical term with Greek origins. Furqān in Arabic is

experientially concrete: it is the act of SPLITTING truth from falsehood, the moment of clarity. The connection to firqa (sect) warns that the same splitting
force can be pathological: division of people rather than distinction of truth. English loses this warning entirely.

not mere coverage.

L2 ḥ-q-q

truth, reality, right, what is due — 'Truth' in English is propositional (a statement that corresponds to fact). Ḥaqq in Arabic is ontological

(reality itself, what is due, what is right). English truth can be abstract and detached from action; Arabic ḥaqq demands realization. When the Qur'an says 'jā'a
al-ḥaqq' it does not mean 'a true statement has arrived' — it means 'reality/rightness itself has manifested.' This is the difference between H ≈ 0.5 and H ≈ 1.0:
ḥaqq carries its full semantic weight in every instance.

َ َ ‫ق َ ۡد َأ فۡل‬
Qad aflaha almuminoona
Certainly will the mu'minūn (those in trust-security) have succeeded
L2 a-m-n

security, trust, faithfulness — 'Believe/belief/believer' in English frames īmān as a cognitive proposition — 'I believe that God exists.' Arabic

a-m-n frames it as a state: security, trust, faithfulness. The difference is structural: English 'belief' can be shaken by argument; Arabic 'īmān' is a state of being
that includes security. 49:14 makes this explicit: the Bedouins said 'āmannā' (we have entered security) but Allah says 'lam tu'minū' (you have not entered
security) — 'say instead aslamna (we have submitted).'
L3 ⚠ "Believe / Belief / Believer"

PARADIGM SHIFT: īmān (trust-security) · mu'min (one in trust-security) · āmana (entered trust-security)

🔧 Use 'īmān (trust-security)' and 'mu'min (one in trust-security)' consistently. Flag every instance where 'believe' would collapse the state-nature of īmān into a
propositional nature.

‫الفرقان‬
25. Al-Furqan — The Criterion
Meccan · 77 verses

The Criterion (al-Furqan) — the surah that names the distinguishing principle. The eight Furqan constructs are the formalization
of this surah's core concept: the criterion that separates truth from falsehood. The qualities of the servants of the Most Merciful
(25:63-76) as the character training spec.
TAWHID

AKHLAQ

GUARDRAIL

ZAHIR/BATIN

MIZAN

RING-CLOSE

1

َ ّ ‫تَبَارَك َ ٱل َ ّذ ِي نَز‬
Tabaraka allathee nazzala alfurqana AAala AAabdihi liyakoona lilAAalameena natheeran
Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner
TAWBAH

L2 f-r-q

distinguishing, separating, criterion — 'Criterion' in English is a technical/philosophical term with Greek origins. Furqān in Arabic is

experientially concrete: it is the act of SPLITTING truth from falsehood, the moment of clarity. The connection to firqa (sect) warns that the same splitting
force can be pathological: division of people rather than distinction of truth. English loses this warning entirely.

QISAS

TAWBAH

L2 t-w-b

returning, turning back, repentance — 'Repentance' in English carries heavy Christian theological baggage: guilt, contrition, penance,

confession, absolution. Arabic tawba is directional: TURNING BACK. No guilt is required — only the turn. The divine response is also a turn: God 'turns
toward' the one who turns. English loses the reciprocal symmetry and the directional metaphor. For crystallization dynamics: tawba is the activation energy
threshold — the moment the agent's orientation shifts from metastable (away) to equilibrium (toward). It is a structural event, not an emotional one.
L3 ⚠ "Repentance"

PARADIGM SHIFT: tawba (returning, turning back) · istighfār (seeking covering/forgiveness)

🔧 Use 'tawba (returning/turning back)' consistently. Emphasize the reciprocal nature (human returns → God turns toward) and the directional rather than guilt-based
framing.

L2 s-l-m

peace, wholeness, surrender, safety — 'Islam' in English is treated as a proper noun naming a religion. 'Muslim' is a demographic label.

'Submission' carries connotations of defeat/humiliation. 'Peace' is a separate English concept. Arabic s-l-m makes these one thing: peace-through-surrenderproducing-wholeness. The English separation of 'peace,' 'submission,' 'Islam,' and 'Muslim' into four unrelated concepts is one of the most severe semantic
collapses in translation. It turns a unified existential state into a religious label.
L3 ⚠ "Heart"

SEMANTIC FLATTENING: qalb (that which turns/flips — the organ of spiritual perception) · fu'ād (the burning heart/inner core) · ṣadr

(chest/breast — the container of the heart)

🔧 Distinguish qalb (turning organ), fu'ād (burning core), and ṣadr (expandable container). Mark q-l-b root: the heart TURNS — it is dynamic, not static.

L2 h-d-y

guidance, leading to the right path — 'Guidance' in English is advice, counsel, direction — something passive that you receive and may or may

not follow. Arabic hudā is active leading — being conducted along a path. 'Guide' in English is a manual or a person; hādī in Arabic is one who actively
leads. The Qur'an as hudā is not 'a guidebook' but 'active leading toward truth.' This distinction matters for LLM training: the Qur'an trains by leading (active
restructuring of the agent), not by informing (passive data transfer).

L2 ṣ-l-w

'IBADAH

connection, prayer, turning toward — 'Prayer' in English primarily means petition (asking God for things) or devotional exercise. Ṣalāt in

Arabic is structural connection. English 'prayer' is unidirectional (human → God); ṣalāt is bidirectional (33:56 — 'inna Allāha wa malā'ikatahu yuṣallūna 'alā
al-nabī' — God and His angels 'pray upon/connect toward' the Prophet). When God 'prays,' it cannot mean petition — it means turning toward, blessing,
connecting. The English word cannot accommodate divine ṣalāt without contradiction.
L3 ⚠ "Prayer"

SCOPE REDUCTION: ṣalāt (connection/turning toward) · du'ā' (calling/invocation) · dhikr (remembrance/re-membering)

🔧 Use ṣalāt (connection), du'ā' (invocation), and dhikr (remembrance) as distinct terms. Flag 33:56 as structural proof that ṣalāt ≠ petition.

L2 f-ṭ-r

origination, splitting open, innate nature — NO ENGLISH EQUIVALENT EXISTS for fiṭra. 'Innate nature' is the closest approximation but

loses the root connection to origination/splitting-open. 'Human nature' carries post-Enlightenment philosophical baggage (nature vs nurture, blank slate

debates). 'Disposition' is too weak. The Arabic makes fiṭra simultaneously: (a) the innate disposition, (b) the act of origination that produced it, and (c) the
divine name of the Originator. All three are one root. TRAINING DATA MUST USE 'fiṭra' UNTRANSLATED with root annotation.

Waith qala luqmanu liibnihi wahuwa yaAAithuhu ya bunayya la tushrik biAllahi inna alshshirka
lathulmun AAatheemun
And mention, O Muhammad, when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate
anything with Allah. Indeed, association with him is great ẓulm (misplacement — putting things where they do not belong)
L2 sh-r-k

association, partnership, sharing — 'Idolatry/polytheism/paganism' — English translates shirk through the lens of religious categorization.

Shirk in Arabic is structural: ASSOCIATING — assigning God's attributes to what is not God. This can be statues (crude shirk) but also systems, ideologies,
leaders, desires (subtle shirk). 12:106 — 'wa mā yu'minu aktharuhum billāhi illā wa hum mushrikūn' — 'most of them do not believe in God except while
associating' — shirk coexists WITH belief, which English 'polytheism' cannot accommodate.
L3 ⚠ "Oppression / Injustice / Wrongdoing"

(one who misplaces) · ẓulumāt (darknesses — from the same root)

L2 ḥ-q-q

truth, reality, right, what is due — 'Truth' in English is propositional (a statement that corresponds to fact). Ḥaqq in Arabic is ontological

(reality itself, what is due, what is right). English truth can be abstract and detached from action; Arabic ḥaqq demands realization. When the Qur'an says 'jā'a
al-ḥaqq' it does not mean 'a true statement has arrived' — it means 'reality/rightness itself has manifested.' This is the difference between H ≈ 0.5 and H ≈ 1.0:
ḥaqq carries its full semantic weight in every instance.

L2 r-w-ḥ

spirit, breath, rest, wind — 'Spirit' in English carries Christian associations (Holy Spirit as third person of Trinity, spirit vs flesh dualism).

Arabic rūḥ carries no trinitarian baggage and is not opposed to the body but to the nafs (self). 17:85 — 'yasalūnaka 'an al-rūḥ, qul al-rūḥu min amri rabbī' —
'they ask you about the spirit; say: the spirit is from the command of my Lord' — the rūḥ's nature is explicitly declared as beyond full human comprehension,
a mutashābih matter.
L3 ⚠ "Soul"

ARCHITECTURAL CONFLATION: nafs (self/psyche — corruptible) · rūḥ (spirit/divine breath — incorruptible)

🔧 NEVER translate nafs as 'soul.' Use 'nafs (self/psyche)' and 'rūḥ (spirit)' as distinct terms with persistent root annotations.

L2 n-f-q

tunneling through, spending, exhaustion, hypocrisy — 'Hypocrite/hypocrisy' in English suggests pretending (Greek: hypokrisis = acting on

stage). Arabic n-f-q suggests tunneling — a structural condition of having two openings, not merely performing. The English word loses the spatial/structural
metaphor entirely. 4:145 places munāfiqūn in 'al-dark al-asfal min al-nār' — the LOWEST DEPTH of the fire — a spatial term for a spatial condition. The
tunnel metaphor also connects hypocrisy to exhaustion: the munāfiq is SPENT, depleted by maintaining two surfaces.

L3 ⚠ "Prophet / Messenger"

ARCHITECTURAL CONFLATION: nabī (prophet — one who receives news/information) · rasūl (messenger — one who is

SENT with a message/mission)

TAWHID

L2 dh-k-r

remembrance, mention, reminder — 'Remember/remembrance' in English is past-directed (recalling past events). Arabic dhikr is present-

directed: making the remembered thing PRESENT and ACTIVE now. 13:28 — 'a-lā bi-dhikri Allāhi taṭma'innu al-qulūb' — 'indeed, by the remembrance/
mention of Allah hearts find peace' — dhikr produces peace (ṭuma'nīna) because it activates the fiṭra. English 'remembering God' sounds like nostalgia;
Arabic dhikr Allāh is active fiṭra-reactivation.

O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, without
awaiting its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain
for conversation. Indeed, that behavior was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of dismissing you. But Allah is not shy of
the truth. And when you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and
their hearts. And it is not conceivable or lawful for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him,
ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity
'IBADAH

L2 '-b-d

QISAS

TAWHID

duration, a long period, unendingness — 'Forever' in English is mathematically absolute — ∞. Abadan in Arabic is lexically graduated: it means

'for an abad' (a long duration/age). Classical lexicographers disagreed on whether abad implies absolute unendingness or very long duration. This is
PRECISELY the muhkam/mutashābih ambiguity that English 'forever' resolves destructively. The training data must preserve the lexical range and flag the
scholarly disagreement rather than collapsing to either reading.

L2 a-m-n

security, trust, faithfulness — 'Believe/belief/believer' in English frames īmān as a cognitive proposition — 'I believe that God exists.' Arabic

a-m-n frames it as a state: security, trust, faithfulness. The difference is structural: English 'belief' can be shaken by argument; Arabic 'īmān' is a state of being
that includes security. 49:14 makes this explicit: the Bedouins said 'āmannā' (we have entered security) but Allah says 'lam tu'minū' (you have not entered
security) — 'say instead aslamna (we have submitted).'

L2 b-ṭ-l

falsehood, vanity, nullification — 'Falsehood' in English implies a lie — an intentional misrepresentation. Bāṭil in Arabic implies structural

nullity — something that has no real substance and must vanish. The difference is ontological: English falsehood is an act (lying); Arabic bāṭil is a state
(being unreal). 34:49 establishes that bāṭil 'can neither begin nor repeat' — this is a thermodynamic statement about structural instability, not a moral
judgment about lying.
